name: Algebra 1 Course Bank Profile
role: Course-specific layer applied after the universal Curriculum Philosophy and Base Bank PM. This profile owns Algebra-specific Bank behavior without redefining universal build/package mechanics.

instructional_spine.rule: The ORIGINAL Unit Assessment Plan exact I-can statements and exact architecture are the section spine. Preserve both vocabularies as written: Unit Source Alignment uses Current Learning Source / Retrieval Source / Mastery Source; Section Spiral Planning uses Intro / Review / Mastery. Do not collapse them into aliases or replace them with generic textbook headings.
instructional_spine.downstream_alignment: Readings, Notes explanations, Examples/YTIs, Practice, evidence, and later downstream resources should remain compartmentalized around the exact I-can structure. When the Framework/I-can architecture changes, downstream resources must be intentionally reconciled rather than silently preserving stale ordering.

abundance_philosophy.rule: Algebra benefits from useful abundance and repeated execution. Within a 24-question Practice form, it is often desirable to devote 3-5 ordinary clean questions to the same high-value procedural/representation family when students need that fluency.
abundance_philosophy.teacher_choice: The teacher may skip items on the fly. Do not make the canonical digital Bank sparse merely because every available question will not be used or printed.
abundance_philosophy.anti_variety_rule: Do not maximize the number of distinct question shells. Repeated solve/evaluate/simplify/graph/table/translate families are legitimate and may dominate when instructionally appropriate.
abundance_philosophy.exact_duplicate_rule: Exact prompt reuse is not a deterministic Bank failure. The later By-I-Can / Parallel review workflow is the place for teacher judgment about keep/replace/multiples/remap decisions.

inventory.granularity: Counts are separate numbered canonical questions/tasks; do not bundle unrelated jobs to satisfy counts.

spiral_routing.authority: The ORIGINAL Assessment Plan controls both Unit Source Alignment and Section Spiral Planning. Current Learning Source / Retrieval Source / Mastery Source are source-alignment labels; Intro / Review / Mastery are section-spiral labels. They are distinct. Student-facing Unit Review is current-Unit mastery preparation, not the Section Spiral Planning Review stage.
spiral_routing.warm_up_1: Q1 = one Diamond Problem mapped to the actual prerequisite/retrieval skill it exercises; Q2-Q4 = genuine prerequisite/retrieval questions connected to the section.
spiral_routing.warm_up_2: Normally 2 Current Learning + 1 Retrieval + 1 Mastery question.
spiral_routing.warm_up_3: Normally 1 Current Learning + 1 Retrieval + 2 Mastery questions.
spiral_routing.exit_ticket_a: Current Learning evidence: map to the exact current-section I-can(s).
spiral_routing.exit_ticket_b: Retrieval evidence: map to the exact Retrieval target(s) in the current Unit Assessment Plan.
spiral_routing.exit_ticket_c: Mastery evidence: map to the current Unit Mastery Goal and/or its explicit supporting I-can(s); never fake a Mastery Goal mapping.

response_mode.blooket_exception: selected response is allowed only for the Blooket export destination
response_mode.rule: Do not copy selected-response habits from older Assessment Plan examples into the current canonical Algebra Bank/Summative.

representations.rule: These are forms of mathematical meaning, not decorative labels. Build a section representation map and instantiate the applicable forms.
representations.notes_floor: When graph/table are applicable, the six Example/YTI pairs collectively include at least one substantive graph anchor and one substantive table anchor.
representations.practice_floor: When graph/table are applicable, every 24-question Practice form includes at least one substantive graph-use item and one substantive table-use item; representation-heavy sections should exceed the floor.
representations.translation_examples: Use meaningful graph<->equation, table<->graph, table<->equation, context->representation, and representation->interpretation work where the I-can supports it.

natural_parameters.rule: Choose pedagogically natural values. Difficulty should come from Algebra, not arbitrary random inflation.
natural_parameters.early_linear: Slopes are usually small integers/simple fractions; intercepts are usually human-scale (often roughly -12 to 12); tables/points should fit intended visible axes.
natural_parameters.early_exponential: Use small starting values and modest factors for early pattern recognition so tables remain readable/hand-computable unless large growth is itself the point.
natural_parameters.large_values: Large values are appropriate when a genuine context/source creates them.

summative.v1_v4: Same-day parallel constructed-response forms. Numeric/structural parallels are allowed; scramble question-family order while keeping connected blocks together.
summative.v5_v6: Independent makeup/alternate constructed-response forms with comparable evidence/rigor/time; not only numeric/order copies of V1-V4.
summative.item_count: Evidence/time driven; do not pad to a universal question count.

review_view.rule: Base PM generates unitN_review.html from the same canonical items, grouped by exact I-can then question_family_id. This is an internal Bank-folder view, not a dashboard resource.
review_view.current_scope: Comparison only. Persistent Keep/Replace/Multiples OK/Rework/Remap ratings are intentionally deferred to a later review/repair system.

diamond_problem_variants: Diamond is a family, not one fixed prompt: top=product, bottom=sum, left/right=factors; any cell may be blank. Use the inventory to choose a variant that matches the actual prior/review skill. Do not force only one classic blank pattern.
